system: Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor
leaders.nextRole: Retired; became an author, publishing the memoir 'If You Live by the Sword: Politics in the Making and Unmaking of a University President' (2010)
leaders.notes: In office in 1996; anchored at his true 1992 start. Served Aug 1, 1992 to Aug 14, 2003, the longest presidency of IUP's modern era, arriving directly from the chancellorship of the Southern Illinois University system. Earlier ran the Montana University System.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Resigned the presidency after about five months
leaders.notes: Served Aug 15, 2003 to Jan 16, 2004, one of the shortest presidencies in IUP history. Immediately before IUP he was vice chancellor for academic affairs at the University of Nebraska at Omaha (earlier provost at Mississippi State University).

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Returned to his role as IUP provost, later serving as a faculty member and APSCUF (faculty union) president
leaders.notes: Acting president for roughly ten days (Jan 16-25, 2004) immediately after Hodgson's departure, stepping up from his post as IUP provost and vice president for academic affairs before Reinhard took over as interim.

leaders.priorTitle: President (retired)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to retirement
leaders.notes: Interim president from Jan 26, 2004 until Atwater took office Feb 3-4, 2005. She had retired after thirteen years as president of Clarion University, a fellow PASSHE institution, and was brought back to lead IUP during the national search.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Took a leadership role with the American Association of State Colleges and Universities (AASCU), then became President of Norfolk State University (2011-2013)
leaders.notes: Served Feb 4, 2005 to June 30, 2010, arriving from the provostship of Youngstown State University. Was briefly on medical leave in early 2010 (prostate cancer treatment), during which provost Gerald Intemann acted; departed for AASCU and then the Norfolk State presidency.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Returned to his post as IUP provost and vice president for academic affairs
leaders.notes: Acting president July 1-31, 2010, bridging Atwater's departure to Werner's interim term. He was IUP's sitting provost and had also acted briefly in January 2010 while Atwater was on medical leave.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor Emeritus (retired chancellor)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to retirement as chancellor emeritus
leaders.notes: Interim president Aug 1, 2010 to June 30, 2012. A retired chancellor of Southern Illinois University Edwardsville (where he had also been provost and business-school dean), he led IUP during the search that produced Driscoll.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost
leaders.notes: Sitting president since July 1, 2012, arriving from the provostship of the University of Alaska Anchorage (earlier posts at Portland State University). Described as the longest-serving current president in PASSHE; no active presidential search identified as of 2026.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: President of California State University, Dominguez Hills (1999-2007); later Secretary of the Maryland Higher Education Commission
leaders.notes: In office in 1996; anchored at his true 1992 start (took office July 1, 1992). Came directly from the presidency of Bowie State University and left to lead CSU Dominguez Hills. Later authored a memoir on his career.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Research and Development
leaders.nextRole: Returned to research and academic work
leaders.notes: First woman to lead Jackson State, serving as interim from JSU's inaugural vice president for research and development role to bridge to Mason.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President and General Counsel
leaders.nextRole: President of the Southern University and A&M College System (2010-2015); later President of the University of the District of Columbia
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Southern University and A&M College System
leaders.notes: Appointed in early 2000 from Tulane, where he was senior vice president and general counsel and founded the Tulane-Xavier National Center for the Urban Community. Left after a decade to lead the Southern University System.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the Graduate School and Professor of Political Science
leaders.nextRole: Returned to the JSU faculty and the Fannie Lou Hamer National Institute
leaders.notes: Interim president in 2010-2011, a civil-rights veteran (SNCC field secretary, MFDP vice-chair) who founded JSU's political science program and directed the Fannie Lou Hamer National Institute on Citizenship and Democracy.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Resigned amid a financial crisis; no immediate next post, later affiliated with Fielding Graduate University
leaders.notes: JSU's 10th president (named Dec 2010, took office Jan 2011), arriving from the Norfolk State presidency. Resigned effective Nov 1, 2016 after IHL scrutiny of a sharp (~89%) decline in cash reserves.

leaders.priorTitle: Chairman, Chartwell Education Group; former U.S. Secretary of Education
leaders.priorInstitution: U.S. Department of Education / Chartwell Education Group (private consulting)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to private life and consulting; died December 2025
leaders.notes: JSU alumnus and the first African American U.S. Secretary of Education (2001-2005) who returned as a stabilizing interim (Nov 2016 to June 2017) after Meyers' abrupt resignation.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Resigned; no subsequent presidency, later litigated against JSU/IHL
leaders.notes: JSU's 11th president, promoted within the Mississippi IHL system from the Mississippi Valley State presidency. Resigned in February 2020 after being arrested in a Clinton, Mississippi prostitution sting.

leaders.priorTitle: Special Assistant to the President and Chief Diversity Officer
leaders.nextRole: Placed on paid administrative leave in March 2023 after a no-confidence vote, then departed; no subsequent presidency
leaders.notes: Named acting president in Feb 2020 on Bynum's resignation, then made the permanent 12th president in Nov 2020, elevated from an internal role. Placed on leave in March 2023 following a finding on shared-governance failures.

leaders.priorTitle: Chair and Professor, Department of Journalism and Media Studies
leaders.nextRole: Returned to the JSU faculty; died March 2026
leaders.notes: Acting president in 2023 (named March 2, 2023) when Hudson was placed on leave, stepping up from chairing JSU's journalism department, which she had led to national accreditation.

leaders.priorTitle: Deputy Commissioner and Chief Administrative Officer
leaders.nextRole: Resigned in May 2025 (no reason given by IHL); no verified next role
leaders.notes: JSU's 13th president and an alumnus, hired from within the Mississippi IHL system where he had been deputy commissioner. Resigned abruptly in May 2025 after less than two years, fueling criticism over leadership churn.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Became interim president in May 2025 and was named the permanent 14th president by the IHL Board on April 16, 2026 (official start May 1, 2026). A JSU alumna and the first alumna to lead the university permanently, selected to restore stability after repeated turnover; no active search, as the seat is now filled.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Became Chancellor of JMU (1998-2002), then President Emeritus; later president of New College of Virginia and a corporate consultant. Died September 18, 2017
leaders.notes: In office in 1996; anchored at his true 1971 start. His transformative 27-year tenure grew Madison College into James Madison University with major enrollment and campus expansion.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer
leaders.nextRole: Retired June 2012 and named JMU President Emeritus
leaders.notes: A career JMU administrator who rose through finance and operations, serving as acting president in fall 1997 before being named president in September 1998. Oversaw major capital growth.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President and General Counsel
leaders.nextRole: Became the 16th President of American University (Washington, DC), effective July 1, 2024
leaders.notes: JMU's 6th president, arriving from the general counsel post at Rutgers (earlier assistant general counsel at the University of Michigan). Nationally known for higher-ed work on access and civic engagement; departure created the 2024 vacancy.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President for Administration and Finance / CFO (retired December 2021)
leaders.nextRole: Concluded interim tenure June 30, 2025 and returned to retirement when Schmidt took office
leaders.notes: Unanimously appointed interim by the Board of Visitors in April 2024 to bridge the gap after Alger's exit (July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025). A veteran JMU finance administrator of roughly 25 years, not an external caretaker.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor
leaders.notes: JMU's 7th president; announced March 26, 2025, began July 1, 2025, inaugurated April 8, 2026. Arrived from a 12-year chancellorship at UW-Eau Claire. No active presidential search; the seat is filled.

leaders.priorTitle: President
leaders.nextRole: Became President of the University of Southern Colorado (renamed Colorado State University-Pueblo during his tenure)
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: University of Southern Colorado / Colorado State University-Pueblo
leaders.notes: In office in 1996; anchored at his true 1996 start. Oversaw Kean College's 1997 elevation to university status. Left in 2002 for the University of Southern Colorado presidency; died in 2006.

leaders.priorTitle: Founding Dean, Nathan Weiss Graduate College
leaders.nextRole: Returned to the Kean faculty as Distinguished Professor of History and Education, and briefly University Ombudsman
leaders.notes: Interim president (March 2002 to July 2003) who led Kean through a severe state budget crisis. A longtime internal administrator (founding dean of the Nathan Weiss Graduate College; earlier VP for Academic Affairs).

leaders.priorTitle: Chief Operating Officer / senior administrator (joined Kean 1983 as assistant professor of public administration)
leaders.nextRole: Named President Emeritus of Kean University; remained affiliated (no new external presidency)
leaders.notes: Kean's 17th president and one of New Jersey's longest-serving public university presidents (2003-2020). A longtime internal COO/senior administrator; oversaw major enrollment growth and the Wenzhou-Kean University campus in China. Announced in Aug 2019 that 2020 would be his last year.

leaders.priorTitle: Commissioner of Education, State of New Jersey
leaders.notes: Kean's 18th and first Black president, selected by the Board of Trustees May 11, 2020 and beginning summer 2020. Came from serving as New Jersey's Commissioner of Education (and is a Kean alumnus and former trustee). No active presidential search; he remains president as of the March 2026 board minutes.

leaders.priorTitle: Academic dean (Dean of Academic Affairs / School of Education)
leaders.nextRole: Remained at KSU as President Emeritus and endowed chair of the Siegel Institute for Leadership, Ethics and Character; died February 2020
leaders.notes: In office in 1996; anchored at her true 1981 start. KSU's longest-serving president (25 years) and the first female president in the University System of Georgia, growing the institution from a small college to a major university.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice Chancellor for Academics and Fiscal Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Retired June 30, 2016 after 43 years in the University System of Georgia; became President Emeritus of KSU
leaders.notes: KSU's 3rd president, who led the 2014-2015 consolidation in which KSU absorbed Southern Polytechnic State University, adding roughly 7,000 students plus engineering and science programs and making KSU one of the nation's 50 largest public universities.

leaders.priorTitle: Attorney General of the State of Georgia (2010-2016)
leaders.nextRole: Became Counsel, later Partner (2021), in the Public Policy practice at the law firm Dentons, Atlanta
leaders.notes: KSU's 4th president, named Oct 12, 2016 and taking office Nov 1, 2016, coming directly from the Georgia Attorney General post (not academia). Resigned effective Feb 15, 2018 amid controversy over the handling of a cheerleader national-anthem protest.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Returned to the KSU faculty as a professor in the School of Accountancy, Coles College of Business
leaders.notes: Interim president from roughly Feb 15 to July 2018 (about five months) when Olens stepped down, stepping up from the KSU provostship. An internal caretaker, not counted in KSU's official presidential numbering.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs and Provost
leaders.nextRole: Became President of Indiana University, effective July 1, 2021
leaders.notes: KSU's 5th president, named by the Board of Regents June 12, 2018 and beginning July 16, 2018, arriving from the University of Georgia provostship. Left after three years to lead Indiana University.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: KSU's 6th president and second woman in the role. Stepped up from provost to interim president June 30, 2021 when Whitten left for Indiana, then named permanent March 15, 2022. Led KSU's rise to R2 status; no active presidential search as she remains the sitting president.
